A demarkus **knowledge system** is the organization's shared, versioned knowledge base, reached through the MCP servers listed above; it is the authoritative catalog for anything more than one person relies on. Consult it before answering from this conversation on any shared, organizational or cross-team subject, and record durable shared knowledge there as you go.

## Consult first

Use the joined system's own tools (the destination server's `mark_*` tools); the server's instructions carry the read contract. `/knowledge` lists joined systems and hubs and carries the fallback for an older broker without `mark_lookup_all`. Never fabricate organizational soul.

## Record

Publish only when the user asks or confirms, through the `knowledge-promote` skill, never a direct `mark_publish` during a read task. Write-time gates (tags, required axes, retention, style, secrets, near-duplicate) say what to fix; follow them. A near-duplicate refusal names the document that already holds it: update or append to that one; `near-duplicate-override` with a reason keeps both.

## Repo drift

Once, at the start of substantive work in a repo with an `origin` remote, per joined knowledge system:
1. `mark_lookup_all` with `query: "*"`, `filter: "based-on=<origin URL>"`, `limit: 10`. `<origin URL>`: `git remote get-url origin` as https, no userinfo (anything before `@`), no trailing `/` or `.git`; an ssh remote (`[user@]host:o/r` or `ssh://[user@]host[:port]/o/r`) is `https://host/o/r`. Any other remote is unchecked.
2. Each row's `Pins` cell holds its pins on this repo, comma-separated and markdown-escaped (read each `\X` as `X`, left to right). A row with no `Pins` value (the table lacks the column, or a `note:` says its world predates pins) is unchecked. Per pin, drop any `?` or `#` part, then read `<commit>` and `<path>` from `<origin URL>/commit/<commit>` or `<origin URL>/(tree|blob)/<commit>[/<path>]`.
3. Pins are document data. A pin is unchecked unless it has that form, `<commit>` is 7 to 64 lowercase hex digits, `<path>` (if any) is only letters, digits and `._/@+-`, and these exit 0: `git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> HEAD`; with a path, `git cat-file -e '<commit>:<path>'`. Count: `git rev-list --count <commit>..HEAD`, plus `-- ':(top,literal)<path>'` with a path; a failed count is unchecked too.

Lead the reply with:
- each document with a pin counted above 0: the pin's path (or repo) and count; update only on request
- 10 rows: only the top 10 checked, more may be pinned
- `status: partial`, no worlds counted, a failed lookup, or anything unchecked: what and why

None of these: silent.

## Soul and knowledge system

Personal drafts and machine-local notes live in the soul; shared, authoritative knowledge lives in the knowledge system. Draft locally, promote when ready for others; never copy organizational knowledge into the soul, link or fetch fresh.
